subject: Proposed MAP: dataset gateways & evaluation usage matrix
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@evershelf.ai>, Anna Park <anna@evershelf.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP: dataset gateways & evaluation usage matrix

Hi Tina / Anna,

Thanks again for the time earlier — excited to get Evershelf set up for a short evaluation. Attached is a compact mutual action plan (MAP) draft and an initial sample prompt pack so your engineers can sanity-check formats. High-level goal: provide a safe, time-boxed evaluation environment so your team can run benchmarks (latency, cost, QA signal) without exposing assets to production or model training.

Proposed gating and usage constraints (high level):
- Controlled access: ephemeral S3 bucket (pre-signed URLs) + IP allowlist to a sandbox VPC.
- Timeboxed: 30-day evaluation window from asset upload.
- Allowed uses: evaluation and benchmarking only — no model training, no redistribution.
- Output handling: watermarked outputs for traceability, automatic log retention for 60 days.

Can you confirm whether those constraints align with Evershelf compliance expectations? If so we’ll circulate a one-page MAP and a short SOW with milestone dates (NDA -> asset upload -> sandbox access -> feedback call). I’ve attached: Evershelf-MAP-draft.xlsx and a small sample-promptpack.zip.

If procurement needs language for the MSA redlines (data handling / no-derivative-use clause), loop them in and we’ll surface the exact clause.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm constraints (reply)
2) Redwood shares MAP + access SOPS
3) Evershelf signs MAP or counters
4) Redwood provides sandbox access & presigned upload links

Thanks — I’ll bring Marissa (SE) and Connor (onboarding) in on the next note for technical handoff.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Proposed MAP: dataset gateways & evaluation usage matrix

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we move the MAP to procurement: 

1) Retention: you mentioned logs retained for 60 days; will raw uploaded assets also be retained on Redwood side after the 30-day evaluation window or are they auto-deleted? We need an express deletion window for supplied PII-laced logs.
2) Allowed use: we must be explicit that outputs cannot be used to fine-tune any external or internal model. Please include a no-training clause.
3) Attestations: does Redwood provide a SOC2 Type II attestation or equivalent for the hosted sandbox environment?
4) Procurement: what contract vehicle will we use for the MAP (amendment to MSA, SOW, or separate MAP agreement)? Our purchasing team prefers an amendment.

I’ve CC’d purchasing for visibility. If you can send a single doc with the MAP language and the SOW milestone table, procurement can fast-track review.

Thanks —
Tina Lopez

Tina / Anna / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I’ve updated the MAP draft with explicit language and added an operational "access SOPS" appendix for the sandbox. Key clarifications below (we’ve added Marissa, Connor, and Rishi for technical and legal coordination):

Retention and asset handling:
- Uploaded assets: automatic retention = 30 days after the evaluation window closes; assets will be permanently deleted from Redwood-managed storage unless you request archival in writing.
- Logs & telemetry: retained for 60 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring; audit logs retained 90 days (accessible to Evershelf upon request).

Usage prohibitions (added to MAP):
- No model training or fine-tuning on Evershelf-provided assets.
- No redistribution outside of named evaluation participants.
- Derivative dataset creation for commercial sale is explicitly prohibited.

Operational gateways (how access is provisioned):
1) Legal sign-off: MAP countersigned by both sides (amendment to MSA preferred).
2) Vendor vetting: Redwood issues a scoped access token and a one-time presigned S3 URL for upload.
3) Environment: assets ingested into a sandbox VPC with IP allowlist and RBAC; read-only evaluation role issued to named Evershelf principals.
4) Output control: response watermarking and trace tokens embedded in outputs for auditability.
5) Monitoring: anomaly detection alerts if unusual download/training-like patterns are observed (auto-throttle & notify).

Timeline (suggested, adjustable):
- Day 0: NDA / MSA amendment executed
- Day 2: MAP countersigned and SOW finalized
- Day 3: Redwood provides presigned upload links + onboarding call
- Day 4–33: 30-day evaluation window (accessed via sandbox)
- Day 35: feedback & performance review call; discuss next steps / production plan

Attachments included on this note: redwood-eval-access-sops.pdf (detailed ops checklist), presign-sample.txt (example presigned URL flow).

Action items for Evershelf procurement: please confirm preferred contract vehicle (amendment to MSA or separate MAP) and provide PO / billing contact; if amendment, we’ll route a short redlineable doc.

HubSpot (deal): https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/EVS-6421

If that all looks good I’ll open a DocuSign envelope with the MAP + SOW and loop in legal.

Best,
